title: One who has compassion (Hebrews 4:14–16)
hookLine: a high priest tempted in all things like us, without sin
tomorrow: The substance of things hoped for

lines: THE HIGH PRIEST, ONCE A YEAR.
cards: Before an operation, a nurse who once had the same surgery can say the same words as one who hasn't: it'll be okay. They land differently, because she's been there.
Hebrews builds much of its argument around a picture from Israel's worship: the high priest, who once a year, on the Day of Atonement, entered the holiest place to seek mercy for the people.
Today the preacher says something surprising about the high priest Christians have.

teach.b: First, who it is: a great high priest who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, so hold fast to what you profess.
Then the surprise: "For we have not a high priest, who can not have compassion on our infirmities: but one tempted in all things like as we are, without sin."
The Greek verb for have compassion is sympathēsai: to suffer with, to feel alongside. Not pity from above; fellow feeling from inside. Hebrews means it.
A chapter later it says that in the days of his flesh he offered prayers and supplications with a strong cry and tears.

teach.h: TEMPTED IN ALL THINGS, WITHOUT SIN.
teach.b: The Gospels show him hungry in the desert, tempted there, exhausted, grieving at a friend's tomb, in anguish in Gethsemane. And yet without sin.
Catholic teaching holds both together: the Council of Chalcedon said he is like us in all things but sin. In this picture, sinlessness doesn't make him distant from the tempted.
Some Christian writers have argued that one who never gave way under temptation felt its full weight, and so knows its full strength.
Then the invitation: "Let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace: that we may obtain mercy, and find grace in seasonable aid."

teach.h: ONE TEMPTED IN ALL THINGS LIKE AS WE ARE.
teach.b: The Greek word for confidence means boldness, the freedom to speak openly. Seasonable aid means help at the right moment, when you need it.
Catholics hear this invitation in personal prayer, before the tabernacle, and in confession, where they believe Christ's mercy meets them through the priest.

how: Catholics bring their weaknesses to Christ in personal prayer, in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament, and in the sacrament of penance, where they believe Christ forgives through the priest.

o: to pity someone from far above
to suffer with, to feel alongside
to forgive a sin once confessed

Hebrews' word for compassion means to suffer with
sympathēsai: fellow feeling from inside, not pity from above.
Hebrews tells believers to approach God's throne fearfully, from far off
"let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace."

games.q: you're ashamed of a weakness and sure God is disappointed. what does Hebrews invite you to do?
o: stay away until you've fixed it.
go with confidence to the throne of grace.
hide it and hope nobody notices.
games.why: "let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace: that we may obtain mercy, and find grace in seasonable aid."

practice: Think of one weakness, the kind you'd rather nobody saw: a temptation that keeps winning, a fear, a failure you keep repeating. Don't hide it, and don't beat yourself up; just hold it up, honestly.
If you pray, bring it to Christ as Hebrews invites, with confidence, to someone who understands; if not, picture telling it to someone who has been exactly there.

wordCard.voice: Sympathesai, to suffer with. Hebrews' picture of Jesus as high priest: tempted in all things like us, without sin, feeling alongside us. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: to suffer with, to feel alongside (Hebrews 4:15).

carryVoice: Your line: he understands. Mercy, and help at the right moment, when you need it. See you tomorrow.
